newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish privatisation will not slow down -- premier.
newsitem.headline: Polish privatisation will not slow down -- premier.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Monday said sales of state assets would not slow down although the current liberal privatisation minister is to be sidelined in a cabinet reshuffle.

"Government policy regarding privatisation will not change," Cimoszewicz told reporters before a cabinet meeting. "In fact the privatisation programme we will discuss today envisages speeding up privatisation next year."

The privatisation ministry, headed by Wieslaw Kaczmarek from the ruling coalition's larger Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) party, will be replaced by a new, more powerful treasury ministry on Tuesday as part of a major government reform.

Kaczmarek will lose the top privatisation job under last week's deal between the ex-communist SLD and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL). The agreement gave the treasury ministry to the Peasant Party's Planning Minister, Miroslaw Pietrewicz.
The prime minister confirmed that he would ask President Aleksander Kwasniewski to officially appoint Pietrewicz, 55, an economics professor.
Kwasniewski has made clear he would like Kaczmarek to be in charge of privatisation, a key element of market reforms initiated after the fall of communism in 1989.

Kwasniewski -- linked to the SLD, which has adopted many liberal policies despite its communist roots -- has suggested that Pietrewicz, whose party colleagues often oppose selling off state assets, was not the best person for the job.
But despite such objections, the president, who has said he would leave cabinet appointments up to the coalition, is widely expected to nominate Pietrewicz.
The Peasant Party has said the coalition deal on Friday, which ended nearly four weeks of rows and threats of a break up, provides for keeping Kaczmarek as a senior official in the treasury ministry.
But Kaczmarek said on Monday he had not been offered any job. "I do not know how the cards have been dealt. I have taken no part in the dealing," he told reporters.

Under the coalition agreement, the SLD will control the new economy ministry, which will replace the industry and foreign trade portfolios, and the powerful ministry of administration and internal affairs.
The two ministries will be created on January 1, 1997, as the second stage of the reform, aimed at streamlining decision-making and reducing the central government's role in the economy.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, a non-party technocrat and the author of the government economic policy, would most probably keep his job, Peasant Party leaders have said.
